# A "#" in column 0 comments a line out of the mkfile. Between recipe lines
# it becomes an empty line, so the recipe continues and its line numbers stay
# the same; before the first or after the last recipe line it is dropped.
# Indented "#" lines are part of the recipe, for the program to handle.

mk -n -p 1 between
cmp stdout between.want

mk -n -p 1 leading
cmp stdout leading.want

mk -n -p 1 after-blank
cmp stdout after-blank.want

# a comment after the last recipe line, then the next rule, works as before
mk -n -p 1 trailing next
cmp stdout trailing.want

# and the recipe runs: the commented-out line does not
mk -p 1 runs
cmp stdout runs.want

-- mkfile --
between:V:
	one
# two, commented out
	three
	# four, kept

	six

leading:V:
# commented out before the recipe
	one

after-blank:V:
	one

# commented out after a blank line
	four

trailing:V:
	one

# --- a section comment ---
next:V:
	next one

runs:V:
	echo one
#	echo two
	echo three
-- between.want --
between: one
          
          three
          # four, kept
          
          six
-- leading.want --
leading: one
-- after-blank.want --
after-blank: one
              
              
              four
-- trailing.want --
trailing: one
next: next one
-- runs.want --
runs: echo one
       
       echo three
one
three
